newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says to ask Nomura to present its case July 24.
newsitem.headline: MOF says to ask Nomura to present its case July 24.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) will ask Nomura Securities Co Ltd to present its case regarding its involvement in a racketeer scandal on July 24, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Friday.

Earlier this week, Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission recommended to MOF that it impose penalties against Nomura for violating the Securities and Exchange Law over a payoff scandal involving a racketeer.
After the recommendations are made, the procedure allows for the firm to present its case to MOF before the ministry decides on any penalties.
Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference that the ministry will ask Nomura about the alleged violations of the Securities and Exchange Law and Commerical Code.
He added he did not know who would represent Nomura.
Mitsuzuka also said the meeting with Nomura will be open to some reporters because of the case's importance to the public, and the need to ensure that the administrative process is transparent.
Mitsuzuka declined to comment on any possible penalties against Nomura, saying only : "we will deal with it strictly".
He also said Japan's trade surplus was unlikely to rise significantly and lead to trade friction.
